course_outline_concepts: n-gram overlap detection: bucket size, cutoff, false-positive/negative tradeoffs
Canary-string + watermark approaches; their limits with paraphrased leakage
Downstream contamination: train data leaked into RM pref data leaked into eval
Contamination reporting conventions: what a defensible memo claims vs doesn't
Live-in-wild contamination: benchmarks leaked onto the web within days of release

sources.what_to_extract: ExactSubstr suffix-array method at 50-token threshold; NearDup MinHash+LSH with 5-gram shingles, 9000 signatures, 20 bands x 450 rows -> Jaccard ~0.8; observed 4.6% LM1B / 3.2% C4 train-test overlap; 10x memorization reduction after dedup. This is the canonical train-test overlap methodology contamination workflows inherit.

Iterative SFT->RS->DPO pipeline where rejection-sampled outputs become next-round SFT data; re-mined from current best checkpoint. Contamination risk: eval prompts leaking through rejection-sampling into RM training pool, then back into SFT. Post-training data disclosure reveals which synthetic pipelines carry the highest contamination exposure.

Dolmino cooldown mix at 50B tokens on top of 3.9T OLMo-Mix-1124. Cooldown is the highest contamination-risk stage because it injects small high-quality pools near end of training. Decontamination must be applied per-stage, not just on the initial corpus.

Dolma 3 Mix ~6T tokens with stronger decontamination vs Dolma 3 (9.3T). OLMo 3 ships decontamination and dedup utilities as public tooling. Multi-stage training flow (base/mid/long-context/SFT/DPO/RLVR) means decontamination must run at every stage with eval-set hashes pinned before each stage.

Data quality as explicit scaling variable; effective sample size framing. Contamination inflates reported benchmark scores, making a contaminated corpus appear to sit on a better scaling curve than it is. Justifies why contamination reporting is non-optional for any scaling-law claim.

External verification + tail-recall metrics for synthetic data; parallel concern for eval contamination of synthesis pipelines. Paraphrased leakage is the tail-of-distribution case n-gram overlap misses; the analog to tail recall is rare-prompt match across train and eval.

Filter cascade: URL dedup -> doc dedup -> lang -> quality -> content/PII -> paragraph dedup. Decontamination slots in as a pinned-set step that runs alongside paragraph dedup with fixed eval-set n-grams. dolma-ngram paragraph dedup = same primitive repurposed for eval-set matching.

Per-snapshot MinHash dedup beats global dedup for downstream accuracy. Implication for contamination: dedup granularity affects contamination recall -- global sig cross-snapshot matches, per-snapshot misses cross-snapshot leakage; use both for eval-set matching.

Adversarial contamination: trigger-conditioned data that survives later safety training. Contamination is not only accidental eval leakage; an adversary can plant trigger-conditioned examples that evade n-gram matching because they are paraphrased variants on the same latent trigger. Motivates canary+watermark design with unpredictable trigger distributions.

AIME and MATH prompts are public -> teacher model (R1) may have memorized; distillation inherits that memorization through traces. Decontamination must run on the distilled trace set against the target eval, not only on the original seed prompts. Concrete example of downstream contamination: train -> RM pref -> eval pathway.

deliverables: figures/contamination-detect.html (self-contained, n-gram size + cutoff slider, paraphrase-leakage panel, ~200-280 lines)
hard_rules: No external CDN references in HTML (inline CSS/JS only)
Quote attested parameter values from raw-data sources; label inferred defaults when not attested
Decontamination pseudocode must reference real primitives: MinHash+LSH, Bloom filter, suffix-array / exact-substring, 5-gram and 13-gram thresholds as attested in sources
Defensible-memo template must enumerate what a contamination report CAN and CANNOT claim
